Sub-class proteomics

Source: R/proteomics-class.R
proteomics.Rd

OmicFlow is constructed around the main superclass omics that in turn is inherited by metagenomics and proteomics, that offer additional fields or methods. The superclass omics contains both public and private methods, only the public componenents are documented, whereas the private methods can be accessed via proteomics$private_methods, which is not supported.

The omics class components use Matrix and data.table in the background for fast loading and data wrangling, these data structures return the data by reference, so does the R6 class, therefore classes in OmicFlow do not create copies of the object unless called via $copy().

All classes needs to be first initialised via the $new() method and require the metaData and countData field components. Alternatively, you can also initialise with only the metaData and later add the other fields via the active binding, but this will not create a back-up and is not advised! For more hands-on examples see Getting Started with OmicFlow.

Additional arguments in proteomics$new()

The proteomics class also offers the loading of a phylogenetic tree as a phylo class (see as.phylo) that can be supplied to treeData. When a treeData is supplied than every class field is arranged according to the tree tip labels.

Input requirements

Every class in OmicFlow requires at least a metaData and countData field to be specified. The metaData must contain a SAMPLE_ID and optionally a SAMPLEPAIR_ID, see section "Metadata validation" below.

The countData can be both a matrix or data frame. If the original contains rownames, then these will become the FEATURE_ID in featureData (automatically created), otherwise a random feature identifier is assigned. If the countData is a filetype or a data frame with both matching sample identifiers in SAMPLE_ID and other additional columns, then these will be automatically split, columns matching the SAMPLE_ID will be placed in the countData, any other columns will be placed in front of the FEATURE_ID column in featureData.

Metadata validation

Every class in OmicFlow begins by validating the sample metadata. This validation checks that sample identifiers match the sample IDs present in the abundance tables.

The validation rules are defined in JSON format in the omics class. Metadata can be supplied as either:

  • A CSV or TSV file.

  • A data.table.

In both cases, metadata must include a header row and follow a one-row-per-sample structure. For file inputs, the header must be on the first line. Columns not described below are permitted and are ignored during metadata validation.

Minimum requirement

The metadata must contain a SAMPLE_ID column.

  • Each row must have a unique, non-empty sample identifier.

  • Sample identifiers cannot contain spaces; use underscores (_) or dashes (-) instead.

Example metadata:


SAMPLE_ID  SAMPLEPAIR_ID  CONTRAST_Treatment  VARIABLE_Age
S1         P1             Drug                42
S2         P1             Placebo             36
S3         P2             Drug                51

Column types and naming rules

Required column

ColumnTypeRules
SAMPLE_IDstringUnique, non-empty, no spaces; one identifier per sample row

Optional standard columns

ColumnTypeRules
SAMPLEPAIR_IDstringOptional; no spaces. Used for samples that are paired or originate from the same individual or subject.

Some functions require a SAMEPLEPAIR_ID in the metaData when paired = TRUE is used. The user can add or remove the SAMPLEPAIR_ID at anytime to the metaData via active binding.

Pattern-based columns

Additional variables can be defined with special column-name prefixes:

  • CONTRAST_...: Grouping or category labels for differential comparisons. For example, CONTRAST_Treatment may contain Drug and Placebo.

  • VARIABLE_...: Numeric or string variables for statistical analysis. For example, VARIABLE_Age may contain values such as 42 and 51.

Pattern-based columns are only used in $autoFlow(). Currently, only columns with the CONTRAST_ prefix are supported.

omics -> proteomics

proteomics$new()

Usage

proteomics$new(
  countData = NULL,
  metaData = NULL,
  featureData = NULL,
  treeData = NULL
)

Arguments

countData

A path to an existing file, Matrix, data.table or data.frame (default: NULL).

metaData

A path to an existing file, data.table or data.frame (default: NULL).

featureData

A path to an existing file, data.table or data.frame (default: NULL).

treeData

A path to an existing newick file or class "phylo", see read.tree (default: NULL).

Returns

A new proteomics object.

Examples

library("OmicFlow")

## Method 1: load from filepath
metadata_file <- system.file("extdata", "metadata.tsv", package = "OmicFlow")
counts_file <- system.file("extdata", "counts.tsv", package = "OmicFlow")
obj <- proteomics$new(
 metaData = metadata_file,
 countData = counts_file
)

## Method 2: Load from data.frame or matrix
n_cols <- 5
n_rows <- 100
n_vals <- n_cols * n_rows
metadata <- data.frame("SAMPLE_ID" = paste0("Sample_", 1:n_cols))
features <- data.frame("FEATURE_ID" = paste0("protein_", 1:n_rows))
counts <- Matrix::Matrix(
 1:n_vals, nrow = n_rows, ncol = n_cols,
 dimnames = list(features$FEATURE_ID, metadata$SAMPLE_ID)
)

obj <- proteomics$new(
 metaData = metadata,
 featureData = features, # optional
 countData = counts
)

## Method 3: you have features and counts in a single data.frame
metadata <- data.frame(SAMPLE_ID = c("S1", "S2", "S3"))
counts <- data.frame(
 S1 = c(2,3,0),
 S2 = c(2,"",1),
 S3 = c(2,1,NA),
 proteins = c("ZEB1", "ZEB2", "MAPK")
)

obj <- proteomics$new(
 metaData = metadata,
 countData = counts
)

library("OmicFlow")

metadata_file <- system.file("extdata", "metadata.tsv", package = "OmicFlow")

obj <- proteomics$new(
 metaData = metadata_file,

)

#> featureData: 0 attributes × 242 features

## Method 2: Load from data.frame or matrix
n_cols <- 5
n_rows <- 100
n_vals <- n_cols * n_rows
metadata <- data.frame("SAMPLE_ID" = paste0("Sample_", 1:n_cols))
features <- data.frame("FEATURE_ID" = paste0("protein_", 1:n_rows))
counts <- Matrix::Matrix(
 1:n_vals, nrow = n_rows, ncol = n_cols, 
 dimnames = list(features$FEATURE_ID, metadata$SAMPLE_ID)
)

obj <- proteomics$new(
 metaData = metadata,
 featureData = features, # optional
 countData = counts
)
#> ✔ metaData template passed the JSON validation.
#> ℹ Checking for duplicated identifiers ..
#> ✔ featureData is loaded.
#> ✔ countData is loaded.
#> 
#> ── <proteomics> object 
#> metaData: 1 variables × 5 samples
#> countData: 5 samples × 100 features
#> featureData: 0 attributes × 100 features

## Method 3: you have features and counts in a single data.frame
metadata <- data.frame(SAMPLE_ID = c("S1", "S2", "S3"))
counts <- data.frame(
 S1 = c(2,3,0), 
 S2 = c(2,"",1), 
 S3 = c(2,1,NA), 
 proteins = c("ZEB1", "ZEB2", "MAPK")
)

obj <- proteomics$new(
 metaData = metadata,
 countData = counts
)
#> ✔ metaData template passed the JSON validation.
#> ℹ Checking for duplicated identifiers ..
